sentences.text:
This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though matter is listed for orders for steps to respondent no.2, since appeal is of year 2017, it was heard on merits.
2. Challenging judgment and award dated 20.07.2017 passed by I Additional MACT and Additional District Judge, Bidar (for short, 'tribunal'), in MVC no.186/2013 this appeal is filed.

3. Sri Deepak V. Barad, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by North East NC:
2023:KHC-K:7313 Karnataka Road Transport Corporation, challenging finding of tribunal regarding contributory negligence and on quantum.
It was submitted that as per claimant, on 24.04.2012, claimant Nagendra was traveling in Maruti Swift Car bearing Reg.no.KA-35/M-8014 from Bidar towards Bijapur.

Near Hallikhed - B cross, a bus bearing Reg.no.KA-38/F-711 belonging to NEKRTC driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed against car and caused The Managing Director vs Nagendra Kawale And Ors on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161622878/
2 accident.

sentences.text: In said accident, claimant was stated to have sustained fracture of 2nd to 6th ribs and fracture of clavicle.

In claim petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against NEKRTC and owner, driver and insurer of car, tribunal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation of Rs.51,000/-.
It was submitted that while passing impugned award, tribunal did not properly consider negligence for causing accident.
It was also submitted that compensation awarded was also excessive as claimant did not examine any Doctor.
On other hand, Sri Manjunath Mallayya Shetty, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.4-insurer of car sought to justify award.

5. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.
6.

From above submission and since NEKRTC is challenging award on negligence as well as on quantum, points that would arise for consideration are:
Point no.(i): Whether finding of tribunal on negligence calls for interference?
Point no.(ii): Whether compensation calls for reduction?

Point no.(i):
7.

In order to establish actionable negligence against NEKRTC, claimant relied on FIR, complaint,
spot panchanama, charge sheet and Motor Vehicle Inspector's report marked as Ex.P1 to P3, P5 and P6 respectively.
Perusal of FIR and charge-sheet would indicate that police after investigation registered FIR and filed charge-sheet against driver of NEKRTC bus.

In absence of rebuttal NC:
2023:KHC-K:7313 evidence, finding of tribunal based on said material would be justified and would not call for interference.
Consequently, point no.(i) is answered in negative.
Point no.(ii):

8. For injuries sustained namely fractures of 2nd to 6th ribs and fracture of clavicle, tribunal awarded Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.1,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental expenses.
For several fractures sustained, said award cannot be stated to be grossly excessive or unjustified.
On other hand, tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of income during laid-up period and amenities.
9. Thus, there is absolutely no merit for challenge on quantum.
Hence, point no.(ii) is answered in negative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
